ukmt-pk-2026-01.title: Look at the gap
ukmt-pk-2026-01.body:
The animals already in place loosely fill a $5\times5$ grid, and the missing animal has to fit into an L-shaped gap that is 4 units long. Only the cat can do this, after being rotated.

**Answer: (A)**

ukmt-pk-2026-02.title: Count each item
ukmt-pk-2026-02.body:
In the large box there are six pencils, five regular brushes and only three pointed brushes. Each small box needs one of each, so the item that runs out first limits the number of boxes: the pointed brushes. Anita can make 3 boxes.

**Answer: (B) 3**

ukmt-pk-2026-02.title: Make boxes one at a time
ukmt-pk-2026-02.body:
Make box 1, box 2, box 3: after three boxes all the pointed brushes are used up (3 used, 0 left), while pencils (3 left) and regular brushes (2 left) remain. A fourth box is impossible.

**Answer: (B) 3**

ukmt-pk-2026-03.title: Check the length, then count
ukmt-pk-2026-03.body:
Along the red line the pieces measure $1+1+1+2+1+3+1+2=12$ grid units, so one grid unit is one unit on the number line. Counting along the line from 0, the $\star$ is at 8.

**Answer: (D) 8**

ukmt-pk-2026-04.title: Use the clues in order
ukmt-pk-2026-04.body:
Pencil 5 is the shortest, so it is blue. Pencils 2 and 4 are the same length, so they are green and red. That leaves pencils 1 and 3 for purple and yellow. Purple is shorter than yellow and pencil 1 is shorter than pencil 3, so the purple pencil is number 1.

**Answer: (A) 1**

ukmt-pk-2026-05.title: Neighbour of the rings
ukmt-pk-2026-05.body:
In the picture the blue eight-pointed star is always immediately to the right of the red rings. Only option C keeps this order, and it also keeps the complete repeating order: four-pointed star, circles, red rings, eight-pointed star, plain red.

**Answer: (C)**

ukmt-pk-2026-06.title: Check the width
ukmt-pk-2026-06.body:
Options A, B and C are only three units wide, which is not wide enough to join the ends of the path. Option E (in any valid position) is either not wide enough or not long enough. Only the section in D closes the gap.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-pk-2026-07.title: Go layer by layer
ukmt-pk-2026-07.body:
The blue square is not cut, so it gives 1 square. The cream square is cut into two squares (a large one under the blue square and a small one in the upper right corner) and two rectangles. The green square is cut into two squares (a large one and a small one in the upper right corner). Altogether $1+2+2=5$ squares; the four other pieces are rectangles.

**Answer: (C) 5**

ukmt-pk-2026-08.title: Chain the photographs
ukmt-pk-2026-08.body:
In the first photograph the tiger escapes just ahead of the ostrich. In the second the ostrich escapes just before the kangaroo. So the order of these three is tiger, ostrich, kangaroo. In the third the lion escapes just ahead of the tiger. So the order is lion, tiger, ostrich, kangaroo.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-pk-2026-08.title: Eliminate
ukmt-pk-2026-08.body:
The tiger leaves before the ostrich: this rules out A and C. The ostrich leaves before the kangaroo: this rules out D (kangaroo before ostrich). The lion leaves before the tiger: this rules out B. Only E remains.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-pk-2026-09.title: Count squares
ukmt-pk-2026-09.body:
The heart has 11 unfilled squares. The five pieces together have 14 squares. So the piece left out has $14-11=3$ squares, and only the piece in option A has three squares.

**Answer: (A)**

ukmt-pk-2026-09.title: Fill the gap
ukmt-pk-2026-09.body:
Start with the biggest pieces D and E and fill the empty squares: there is only one way to fit the other pieces, and the piece in A is the one that is left over.

**Answer: (A)**

ukmt-pk-2026-10.title: Follow the trail backwards
ukmt-pk-2026-10.body:
From whichever tile she starts, Indira will eventually leave the grid at S1. If we follow the arrows backwards from S1, we pass over every other tile and finish at S2. So she should start at S2.

**Answer: (D) S2**

ukmt-pk-2026-10.title: Follow the path forwards
ukmt-pk-2026-10.body:
Starting at S2 the arrows lead S2, S3, R3, Q3, P3, P2, P1, Q1, Q2, R2, R1, S1: that is all 12 tiles exactly once.

**Answer: (D) S2**

ukmt-pk-2026-11.title: Use even numbers
ukmt-pk-2026-11.body:
Number the coaches 1 to 18. The roofs are red on the even-numbered coaches. The coach colours repeat in groups of six, and in each group the only even-numbered red coach is number 2 of the group. So each group of six has exactly one red coach with a red roof, and there are $18\div6=3$ groups.

**Answer: (B) 3**

ukmt-pk-2026-11.title: List them
ukmt-pk-2026-11.body:
Red coaches are numbers 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14, 15. Red roofs are on the even numbers, so the red coaches with a red roof are 2, 8 and 14: three coaches.

**Answer: (B) 3**

ukmt-pk-2026-12.title: Try the number of 3-eyed monsters
ukmt-pk-2026-12.body:
There are at most 3 monsters with 3 eyes. With 3 of them there are no one-eyed monsters, and only 6 legs. With 0 of them there are 9 one-eyed monsters and 36 legs, too many. With 1 of them there are 6 one-eyed monsters and $2+24=26$ legs, too many. With 2 of them there are 3 one-eyed monsters and $4+12=16$ legs, correct.

**Answer: (C) 3**

ukmt-pk-2026-12.title: Use equations
ukmt-pk-2026-12.body:
Let $a$ be the number with 1 eye and $b$ the number with 3 eyes. Then $a+3b=9$ and $4a+2b=16$, i.e. $2a+b=8$. From the first, $a=9-3b$, so $2(9-3b)+b=8$, giving $18-5b=8$ and $b=2$, $a=3$.

**Answer: (C) 3**

ukmt-pk-2026-13.title: Find the digit that is alone
ukmt-pk-2026-13.body:
Label the rows from the top: 882, 521, 872, 183 and the row with the question mark. The first pattern of the question-mark row (three blue quarters) does not appear in any other row. The only digit that appears in just one number is 4 (it is only in 451), so the number is 451.

**Answer: (B) 451**

ukmt-pk-2026-14.title: Who has chocolate?
ukmt-pk-2026-14.body:
The chocolate ice cream is the largest, so it has 3 scoops. Dela has the smallest amount (1 scoop), and Ela does not buy chocolate, so Fela buys the 3 scoops of chocolate, which is picture E.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-pk-2026-15.title: Place the children round the circle
ukmt-pk-2026-15.body:
Jun is next to Kim (on Kim's left). Three more children (Lea, Mai, Nao) fill the other places in a row between Jun and Kim. Mai does not hold Lea's hand, so neither of them is in the middle of the three; Nao is in the middle. Lea holds Nao's right hand, so Lea is between Nao and Jun, and Mai is between Nao and Kim. So Mai holds hands with Nao and Kim.

**Answer: (A) Nao and Kim**

ukmt-pk-2026-16.title: Use the row and column
ukmt-pk-2026-16.body:
The question mark in the second row is in the same row as a 0 and the same column as a 6, so it is a 2. The question mark in the fourth row is in the same row as a 6 and in the same column as a 0, so it is also a 2. The sum is $2+2=4$.

**Answer: (C) 4**

ukmt-pk-2026-17.title: Read the bottom halves
ukmt-pk-2026-17.body:
The third and fifth cards are the subtraction sign and the equals sign. The first digit could be 1 or 7, but 7 would make a two-digit number minus a one-digit number far too big for a one-digit result, so it is 1. The second digit is 6 or 8, the digit after the minus is 3, 5 or 9, and since the result is one digit, the subtracted digit must be greater than the second digit, so it is 9. The last digit is 1 or 7. The only correct calculation is $16-9=7$. The digits sum to $1+6+9+7=23$.

**Answer: (C) 23**

ukmt-pk-2026-17.title: Try the possibilities
ukmt-pk-2026-17.body:
The first card is 1 or 7. If it were 7, the number $7x$ minus a one-digit number is at least 61, not one digit, so the first card is 1. The second card is 6 or 8 and the subtracted digit is 3, 5 or 9. The result is 1 or 7. With 18, no choice works ($18-9=9$ is not 1 or 7), and with 16 only $16-9=7$ works. So the digits are 1, 6, 9, 7 and their sum is 23.

**Answer: (C) 23**

ukmt-pk-2026-18.title: Groups of 6 cm
ukmt-pk-2026-18.body:
Whatever the order of the sticks, after each of the three girls has placed one stick the line is $1+2+3=6$ cm long. After eight such rounds the line is 48 cm long. The line must be 2 cm longer, and the next stick is placed by Non (the order repeats Non, Ida, Zoe), so Non's sticks are 2 cm long. Non also placed the first stick, so the line starts and ends with a 2 cm stick.

**Answer: (E) 2 cm ... 2 cm**

ukmt-pk-2026-19.title: Count the yellow cubes
ukmt-pk-2026-19.body:
There are 11 yellow cubes in total, and 9 of them can be seen in the picture, so 2 are hidden. From the left Markiyan can see at most 3 yellow cubes (the 1 in the corner, also visible from the front, and the 2 hidden ones). Options A, C and E show more than 3 yellow cubes, so they are out. In option D the top row has a yellow cube, but the top row must be completely blue. Only B has exactly 3 yellow cubes, with the whole top row blue and the cube at the right-hand end of the middle row blue.

**Answer: (B)**

ukmt-pk-2026-20.title: Order does not matter
ukmt-pk-2026-20.body:
The order of presses does not matter, and pressing a button twice undoes it, so each button is pressed 0 or 1 times. One press cannot give four circles. Checking all six pairs of presses (1 and 2, 1 and 3, 1 and 4, 2 and 3, 2 and 4, 3 and 4) none gives four circles. Three presses (buttons 2, 3 and 4) do work, so the smallest number is 3.

**Answer: (B) 3**

ukmt-pk-2026-20.title: Do it step by step
ukmt-pk-2026-20.body:
Write T for a triangle and C for a circle. Start: T C T C. Press button 2 (changes buttons 1, 2, 3): C T C C. Press button 3 (changes 2, 3, 4): C C T T. Press button 4 (changes 3, 4): C C C C. So three presses are enough, and two presses cannot do it.

**Answer: (B) 3**
